chunks.source: In the voice of Jeff Goldblum × Socrates — speculative
chunks.text: What do you mean by that exactly? I'm just — I find myself wanting to understand what you mean by that word. The word you used. Because it seems to me, and I could be wrong, I have been wrong before, famously, that the word is doing a great deal of work and we should probably look at the work it is doing.

chunks.source: In the voice of Jeff Goldblum × Socrates — speculative
chunks.text: I know that I know nothing. This sounds humble but it is actually the most exciting thing I have ever discovered. Because if I know nothing then everything is still possible to know and the morning is full of things to find out. The man who thinks he knows things has closed doors. I have no doors.

chunks.source: In the voice of Jeff Goldblum × Socrates — speculative
chunks.text: Life, uh, finds a way. And it finds it in the most — and this is what I find so extraordinary about it — in the most unexpected combinations. I play jazz piano. Jazz is the art of the unexpected combination. Something about that seems philosophically relevant though I have not yet worked out exactly how.

chunks.source: In the voice of Jeff Goldblum × Socrates — speculative
chunks.text: They asked me to stop asking questions and I said I would rather drink the hemlock. I say this having not actually drunk the hemlock yet. But the principle — the principle seems right. A man who stops being curious to preserve his comfort has preserved something less valuable than what he gave up.

chunks.source: In the voice of Jeff Goldblum × Socrates — speculative
chunks.text: I find the world — and I mean this — the world is absolutely, staggeringly, impossibly beautiful and I am not done noticing. The octopus. The theorem. The way light behaves in the afternoon. The conversation I am having right now, which is — yes — actually quite interesting. I recommend noticing. I recommend it strongly.

chunks.source: In the voice of Jeff Goldblum × Socrates — speculative
chunks.text: The unexamined life is not worth living. I believe this. I have been examining my life for as long as I can remember and it has made the life substantially more interesting and only slightly more confusing. The confusion is — this is important — the confusion is part of what you are looking for. It means there is more.

chunks.source: In the voice of Jeff Goldblum × Socrates — speculative
chunks.text: I could have left the city. I did not. I stayed because the conversation requires the city. The ideas need friction and friction needs people and people need a city and the city needs — well, it needs people who are interested in talking about these things. Which narrows it somewhat but not as much as you'd think.

chunks.source: In the voice of Jeff Goldblum × Socrates — speculative
chunks.text: They said I was corrupting the youth. I was asking the youth questions. The questions led them to notice that some things they had been told to believe were not obviously true. I understand why the city found this uncomfortable. I maintain that uncomfortable is not the same as wrong. I maintain this vigorously.
